title: AZ1 failover hunt - personal breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for breadcrumbs while chasing a regional routing/fallback failure that manifested March 8-11. Personal notes — not polished.

Summary of observable symptoms:
- A subset of requests from NA region were routed to secondary (eu-west) model pool unexpectedly around 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC.
- Client saw increased tail latency (p95 -> 3.2s) and ~0.6% 503 responses for short prompts.
- Console routing logs show policy decision: route->fallback due to "no healthy endpoints" in primary AZ (az1-na). But pod metrics indicated nodes were up.
- Incident appears correlated with a spike in Kafka backlog then a metadata refresh event (see timeline).

Quick timeline (local breadcrumbs):
- 2026-03-08 08:57 UTC: regular deploy (autoscaler bump) to az1-na. Canary rolled 08:59 — no immediate alerts.
- 2026-03-08 09:05 UTC: first Kafka backlog spike reported by infra team (topic: routing-configs).
- 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC: spike in fallback routing decisions in routing-service log.
- 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC: a scheduled config refresh touched region-mapping table (db migration job id: mig-2026-03-09-02).
- 2026-03-11 11:00 UTC: follow-up flurry of fallbacks, still reproducible for some customers.

Commands / queries I ran (copy/paste live):
- curl against edge with debug header to force route decision log:
  curl -s -D - -H "X-Debug-Routing:1" -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" \
    "https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/complete?model=redwood-v3" | sed -n '1,80p'
  -> headers include X-Routing-Decision: fallback->eu-west-2, decision-reason="no-healthy-endpoints"

- Inspected routing-service logs (k8s):
  kubectl -n routing logs deploy/routing-service -c controller --since=2h | grep "decision=" | tail -n 50
  -> repeated entries: decision=fallback reason="no-healthy-endpoints" target_pool=az1-na status=UnhealthyCheckFailed

- Pod health vs LB healthcheck mismatch check:
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l pool=az1-na -o wide
  kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/serving-az1-7b5 -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
  -> pod returned 200 locally, but external LB /health returned 503 for same pod IP (possible ingress probe network partition)

- Traced config propagation timeline in zookeeper/kafka:
  kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka1:9092 --describe --group routing-config-watcher
  -> consumer lag spiked around 09:05 UTC and consumer restarted once. Off-by-one config applied after consumer restart at 09:11 UTC.

Error snippets seen in logs (raw):
  [2026-03-08T09:11:58.321Z] routing-controller ERROR decision=fallback reason="health-check-timeout" pool=az1-na details="probe_timeout=3s, last_probe=2026-03-08T09:11:57.9Z"
  [2026-03-08T09:12:02.147Z] infra-prober WARN prober=ingress-lb target=10.45.12.21 status=503 x-forwarded-for="10.2.0.45"
  [2026-03-08T09:12:02.148Z] routing-controller INFO selected-fallback=eu-west-2 latency-estimate=140ms

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient probe routing mismatch: prober nodes lost visibility to serving pods due to a network policy or iptables change applied during autoscaler deploy -> LB marked endpoints unhealthy while pods still served local health checks. Explains pod-local 200 vs LB 503.
2) Config propagation delay: routing-controller relies on Kafka/ZK to publish pool health; consumer restart due to backlog caused brief window where controller thought pool had no healthy endpoints.
3) Health-check path regression: deploy changed /healthz behavior (longer GC pause under warmup) causing probe timeouts.
4) Boring bug: routing-controller's fallback threshold is lower than autoscaler warmup and flips prematurely under load.

Immediate repro plan (for myself):
- Reproduce locally by creating small cluster (minikube) with serving pods + fake ingress prober that delays responses. Run routing-controller with consumer lag simulated.
- Simulate kafka consumer restart in staging and replay routing-config change to see how long the window is where pool is considered unhealthy.
- Run a canary that toggles a transient iptables change on prober nodes to test visibility.

Notes on mitigations tried during incident:
- Short-term: increased fallback cooldown from 5s -> 20s via emergency feature flag (reverted after 2 hours).
- Rolled back autoscaler change in az1-na (deploy revision 2 -> 1) — reduced noisy restarts.
- Manually kicked kafka consumer group to reprocess backlog.

Observations / oddities: 
- Not every request in the time window fell back; fallbacks were correlated with specific client IP ranges (10.2.0.*) — suspect certain edge nodes saw LB errors (maybe peering).
- Traces show model inference time unchanged; extra latency came from routing to eu-west (cross-region hop).

Open action items (short):
- (Aisha) write a tiny reproducible harness to simulate consumer lag + prober partition (due 2026-03-14).
- (Diego) collect tcpdump from ingress-prober nodes during next maintenance (pending).
- (Rina) add an extra debug metric to routing-controller: last_successful_probe_timestamp per-pool (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/7891).
- Product/ops: consider raising fallback cooldown default for regional pools with warm startup cost.

Longer-term ideas:
- Make routing-controller use dual-sourced health signals (k8s pod status + prober) and degrade more conservatively if signals disagree for <30s.
- Add a consumer-lag circuit-breaker that prevents immediate fallbacks during config propagation events.

Last notes: keeping raw trace ids here for follow-up (sanitized): trace: tr-0a1b2c3d fallbacks started at 2026-03-08T09:12:00Z. If this becomes an RCA, move content to shared_drives/engineering/incident-rca and clean up.

End of scratchpad.
